standards: Output only the translation in English, with one line per source line. Retain the speaker, direction, negation, questions, and revisions of expectation. Keep the concrete images and meaningful repetition. Do not fabricate details. Use concise poetic English. Meaning takes priority over rhyme.
reference: Reference note: In classical Chinese verse the speaker can be implicit. Resolve viewpoint only as the text supports it. Parallel clauses often preserve contrasts of place, time or emotion. Repetition can carry rhythm and force. English may name a subject only where the source licenses it.
boundary: Boundary example, unrelated to the target: 虽归未见君 -> Though I have returned, I have not seen you. Avoid I returned and saw you, which reverses the negative. Example: 隔岸灯明 -> Across the bank the lamps are bright. Do not add an unseen village or a reason for the lamps.
